description: Generate a slide-deck-quality SIPOC diagram: five equal columns headed by big coloured letters, Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs and Customers, with chevrons between them for the flow. Suppliers, inputs, outputs and customers are stacked cards; the process is 2–7 numbered step boxes joined by down arrows, with an optional process name and optional "Starts when" and "Ends when" boundaries. Choose it for Lean and Six Sigma project scoping (the Define phase of DMAIC), process-improvement kick-offs, quality and ISO documentation, and any slide that frames a process by who feeds it and who it serves; use a chevron process instead for a simple left-to-right sequence of phases with no inputs or outputs, an issue tree to break a problem into causes, and a timeline when dates matter. Limits: 1–7 steps (2 or more expected), up to 8 items in each of the other four columns; keep each item to a short phrase and start steps with a verb. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

inputSchema.description: A SIPOC diagram: five columns (Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, Customers) that scope a process from who feeds it to who it serves.

colors.description: Optional colour overrides per column, keyed by its letter, e.g. {"p": "#0f766e"}. Columns without one take the palette colours in order: S the first, I the second, P the third, O the fourth, C the fifth.

c.description: Hex colour for the Customers column.

i.description: Hex colour for the Inputs column.

o.description: Hex colour for the Outputs column.

p.description: Hex colour for the Process column (its letter, step numbers and step boxes).

s.description: Hex colour for the Suppliers column, e.g. "#4f46e5".

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

customers.description: Who receives the outputs (0–8), one card each, e.g. ["Customer", "Finance"]. Internal teams count as customers too.

end.description: Optional end boundary: the event that completes the process, shown below the steps as "Ends when …", e.g. "Payment is received". Omit for none.

inputs.description: What the suppliers provide to the process (0–8), one card each, e.g. ["Purchase order", "Stock levels"].

numbered.description: Number the process steps 1, 2, 3… in coloured circles. Default true; false shows plain step boxes.

outputs.description: What the process produces (0–8), one card each, e.g. ["Shipped order", "Invoice"].

palette.description: Hex colours applied in order to items that have no colour of their own. Pass the user's brand colours here when they name them. Default: indigo, sky, emerald, amber, red, gray.

process.description: Optional name of the process, shown in bold at the top of the Process column, e.g. "Order to cash". Omit for none. Wraps to two lines, then truncates.

start.description: Optional start boundary: the trigger that begins the process, shown above the steps as "Starts when …", e.g. "Customer places an order". Omit for none.

steps.description: Required: the high-level process steps, top to bottom (1–7, ideally 4–7; fewer than 2 renders with a warning, extras are dropped with a warning). Each is a step box joined to the next by a down arrow, e.g. ["Receive order", "Check credit", "Pick and pack", "Ship", "Invoice"]. Start each with a verb.

suppliers.description: Who provides the inputs (0–8; extras are dropped with a warning), one card each, e.g. ["Customer", "Sales team", "Warehouse"]. Short phrases; long ones wrap onto up to four lines.

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400, default 1280, which suits a 16:9 slide). PNG output renders at 2x. Height is computed from the tallest column.

inputSchema.title: SIPOC Diagram
